mechanism_narrative: A sustained low level of the federal funds rate relative to historical averages compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This relationship holds regardless of the current economic cycle.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day S&P 500 returns falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A labor market tightness signaled by unemployment rate falling below 4.0% indicates strong economic growth and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when UNRATE is below 4.0% over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals robust consumer spending and economic expansion, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through improved corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: The joint signal (both HOUST and RSAFS rising) fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances, or the interaction term in a regression model has a non-significant coefficient (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a supply-constrained economic cycle (indicated by low industrial production growth), a decline in INDPRO signals worsening supply conditions and rising inflation, which triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors price in higher risk and potential monetary tightening.
failure_condition: In periods classified as supply-constrained (based on INDPRO growth < 0.5% annually), the 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained inflation rate exceeding 2.5% (CPIAUCSL > 2.5%) signals rising price pressures that prompt monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as higher interest rates reduce equity valuations.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5%, the 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) relative to its 12-month moving average signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to stronger corporate profit growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for UNRATE as a predictor of 20-day S&P 500 returns falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between UNRATE and 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals a monetary policy tightening cycle amid rising inflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the real cost of capital rises and growth expectations decline.
failure_condition: The joint signal (both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL rising) fails to produce negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances, or the interaction term in a regression model has a non-significant coefficient (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion (characterized by high consumer spending growth), a sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) signals strong economic momentum and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate continued growth before a potential policy tightening.
failure_condition: In periods classified as late-cycle expansion (based on GDP growth > 2.5% and unemployment < 4.5%), the 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when RSAFS is rising.
